title: Tuna (Ahi or Yellowfin), Frozen, Wild Caught

content.title: About
content.content: Ahi (yellowfin) tuna is a large oceanic fish caught in the wild and flash‑frozen to lock in freshness, flavor, and nutrients. It is a rich source of high‑quality protein, omega‑3 fatty acids, and B‑vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Yellowfin tuna can grow over 2 m long and weigh more than 150 kg.
Wild‑caught tuna is considered more environmentally sustainable than farmed fish because it feeds on natural prey.
Freezing at –30 °C preserves up to 90 % of its nutrients.
Tuna is a staple in sushi, sashimi, and many gourmet dishes.
In Japan, tuna is regarded as the "king" of seafood.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids support heart health, reduce inflammation, and promote brain function.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Tuna provides all essential amino acids needed for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B12, B6, and niacin help maintain energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Selenium, magnesium, and potassium in tuna contribute to antioxidant protection and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many meat products, tuna contains relatively little saturated fat.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: Wild tuna can accumulate mercury; pregnant women and young children should limit intake.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood.

items.title: Potential parasites
items.content: Improper storage can allow parasites to develop despite freezing; follow storage guidelines.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tuna can be grilled, baked, pan‑seared, or enjoyed raw in sushi and sashimi. Thaw in the refrigerator, pat dry, and season with lemon, soy sauce, ginger, or fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen tuna at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed, use within 1–2 days and store in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C. Do not leave the fish at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
